title: Capacity Constrained Influence Maximization in Social Networks

problem.claim: Influence maximization must account for the limited capacity of individuals to consume and interact with content in real-world scenarios.

gap.claim: Existing influence maximization solutions produce sub-par results with high computational demands in scenarios where initial adopters are likely to be friends of influencers.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes capacity constrained influence maximization (CIM), which selects a limited number of influential friends for each initial adopter to reach more users.
The paper designs two greedy algorithms, MG-Greedy and RR-Greedy, with a stated 1/2-approximation ratio.
The paper introduces RR-OPIM+, a scalable implementation with a stated (1/2-ε)-approximation and near-linear running time.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive evaluation of 9 approaches on 6 real-world networks, with their solutions outperforming all competitors in result quality and running time.
The authors report that deploying RR-OPIM+ in online game scenarios improves the baseline considerably.

narrative_sequence.summary: Influence maximization selects a small number of influential individuals to maximize information spread and has applications in multiple fields.
Real-world implementation is challenged by individuals' limited capacity to consume and interact with content, including limited friend interactions in online gaming.
Initial adopters may be friends of influencers rather than influencers themselves, while existing solutions may be low-quality and computationally demanding.
The paper proposes CIM and develops greedy algorithms and a scalable implementation with stated approximation and running-time guarantees.
The authors report comparative network evaluations and an online gaming deployment in which their approaches improve reported outcomes.

source_observation.claim: Influence maximization may need to model the content-consumption and interaction capacities of individuals.

interpretation.claim: Adding capacity constraints can change the formulation of a diffusion or influence-selection problem.

application.claim: When applying influence or diffusion methods to capacity-limited social or interaction networks, define constraints around who can consume, interact with, or transmit content.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the capacity-constrained formulation is appropriate beyond the described scenarios.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal CIM objective, constraints, or diffusion model.
The abstract does not provide experimental datasets, parameter settings, or detailed comparison results.
The abstract does not establish proof details for the approximation ratios or running-time claims.
